title: Request and read a status report
goal: Request a Pro-finder status report and interpret it correctly, including when its position and time are not current.
prerequisites: The Pro-finder is operational and you know the number of its installed Nano-SIM.
Your telephone number is saved as an authorised destination number. Non-authorised numbers receive status messages but cannot request reports.
You know the operating-mode selector position because it determines whether a call requests a report and which voltages the report contains.

warnings.text: Do not call the Pro-finder in operating modes 2 and 3 merely to check its status. In these modes a call is a switching action: it changes the WiPro III (safe.lock) to its next state. A status report is then only the confirmation of that state change.

If a report says there is no GPS reception, the transmitted position is the last valid one, not the current one. It can be arbitrarily old and need not be the vehicle's present location. Do not rely on it for locating the vehicle.

Do not interpret the UTC time as the sending time. It is the time of the most recently received position. Without GPS reception, it can be much older than the report without the report explicitly flagging its age.

Every SMS sent by the Pro-finder incurs a charge set by your network provider. Every SMS or call used to control the system produces a status SMS. Modes 4 to 7 also have automatic reports; the operating-mode table additionally lists intervals for C and D.

steps.text: Check which position is selected on the operating-mode selector.
From your authorised telephone number, call the number of the Nano-SIM installed in the Pro-finder. Do not use a call as a status-only request in operating modes 2 or 3.
steps.expected: The Pro-finder ends the call and sends a status report, subject to the operating-mode exceptions described in this task.

steps.text: The source also permits a status request by SMS to the Pro-finder number. This draft does not reproduce the required command text because the device command language remains unresolved; use the call route only where the selected operating mode makes it safe.
Wait for the response. If the vehicle is in a building or another place without GPS reception, the Pro-finder waits up to ten minutes for a valid position before sending the report.

Read the SMS line by line using the field table below. Depending on the operating mode, it can include UTC, position, speed, GPS state, nearby temperature, outputs A and B, supply voltage U1 and measurement-input voltages U2 to U5.

sources.region: Chapter 4, field list and status-report example

steps.text: Before acting on the report, check the GPS statement and UTC time. With no current GPS reception, both position and time relate to the last valid position rather than the report's sending time.

expected_result: You receive a status report by SMS and interpret its UTC time, position, speed, outputs, GPS state and nearby temperature. Depending on the operating mode, the report also contains U1 and measurement inputs U2 to U5. If GPS reception is unavailable, you treat the transmitted position as the last valid and potentially outdated position.

error_cases.problem: A phone call produces no status report.
error_cases.correction: First check the operating mode. For positions 2 and 3, the table shows a dash in the report column, while sections 1.3 and 5.1 say the call changes WiPro III (safe.lock) and produces a report after a successful change. This contradiction is unresolved. For E and F, merged table cells give no call behaviour at all. Also verify that the caller is an authorised destination number.

sources.region: Operating-mode table, positions 2, 3, E and F

error_cases.problem: The status report arrives only after several minutes.
error_cases.correction: This can be expected without GPS reception. The Pro-finder waits up to ten minutes for a valid position, then sends the last received position. Section 5.3 omits this delay; it appears only in section 5.7.

error_cases.problem: Instead of a status report, the reply says the command was invalid.
error_cases.correction: The SMS text was not recognised. The device reply lists possible commands, but this draft deliberately omits them because their valid language and spelling remain unresolved. Request the report by phone only in an operating mode where a call does not change another system state.

error_cases.problem: The report states that there is no GPS reception.
error_cases.correction: The Pro-finder has no valid current GPS position and sends the last valid position instead. Treat it as outdated and request another report later.

error_cases.problem: The UTC time is far in the past.
error_cases.correction: It is not the sending time; it belongs to the last received position. During an alarm and while the engine is running, the Pro-finder continually requests a position, so an old time indicates how long GPS reception may have been absent.

error_cases.problem: The report contains fewer voltage values than expected.
error_cases.correction: The operating mode determines the fields. Positions 0, 2, 8, A and B list none of U1 to U5; 1 and 3 list U1 and U2; 4 to 7 and 9 list all five. C to F have no separate voltage statement because their cells are merged with neighbouring columns.

error_cases.problem: Status reports arrive without a request.
error_cases.correction: The source gives two reasons. Modes 4 to 7 send automatic reports every 15 minutes, 60 minutes, 6 hours or 24 hours. C and D show 90 seconds and 8 minutes in the same column, but their incomplete notes concern GPS searching, so the effect is unclear. A successful output change or call-controlled WiPro III (safe.lock) change also produces a status report.

sources.region: Sections 5.5.1 to 5.5.3, replies after output changes

figures.alt: Example status report shown as a black SMS bubble with twelve data items.
figures.long_description: A black speech bubble with white text contains WiPro ON, Fence ON, a UTC time, a map-service address with coordinates, speed, U1 to U5 voltage values, and output states A and B. The address and coordinates are deliberately omitted here. The prose names temperature and GPS status, and the field list names Pos, but none appears in the printed example. Conversely, the source does not explain what ON means in the WiPro and Fence lines.
steps_text: The first two lines show WiPro and geofencing states; the source does not define ON there.
UTC is followed by position and speed.
U1 is the supply voltage and U2 to U5 are measurement-input voltages.
A and B show the two output states.
